id: NZSQ — Strings in the Earth & Air-Te Whare Whakarauika Wellington Town Hall-Wellington NZ
name: NZSQ — Strings in the Earth & Air
venue: Te Whare Whakarauika Wellington Town Hall
long_description:
A concert of traditional Irish airs and folk melodies will be presented at a concert at the newly opened Wellington Town Hall in April 2027. Join Tom Delany and Dave Flynn for traditional and contemporary works in NZSQ — Strings in the Earth & Air. Tom Delany will play the uilleann pipes, while Dave Flynn will be on the guitar. ‘Uilleann’ means ‘elbow’ in Irish. The uilleann pipes are powered by the elbow, pumping air instead of the Scottish bagpipes that use the lungs. 

The concert takes its name from James Joyce’s poetry collection ‘Chamber Music’. Most of the poems in the collection revolve around the twin themes of love and music. ‘Strings in the earth and air’ is the poem that opens the collection. The concert forms part of New Zealand String Quartet’s In Collaboration series. With roughly one in six Kiwis being of Irish heritage, there are enduring connections between Ireland and Aotearoa. This concert brings those ties to life through poetry, song, and strings.

Tom Delany plays uilleann pipes, guitar, and bouzouki, and sings. As a founding member of Irish ensemble FOURWINDS, he has toured the world. He is known for playing traditional Irish music in a daring, free-flowing style. Dave Flynn is a composer and guitarist who offers a unique blend of Irish trad, minimalism, and jazz. His work has been performed by leading ensembles in venues across the globe.

id: Blossom Valley-Aston Norwood Gardens, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
name: Blossom Valley
venue: Aston Norwood Gardens, Wellington, New Zealand
long_description:
Hosted by Aston Norwood Gardens, 350 Sakura cherry trees burst open at this springtime celebration. Visitors travel from Japan and Australia for the peak bloom. The 14-acre property offers endless photo opportunities. Daytime brings out the natural colours, while the After Dark experience illuminates the valley. Feeling peckish? There are plenty of delicious onsite refreshments. The regal Duke Restaurant & Bar hosts high tea and a refined dinner. Meanwhile, nestled in the gardens, The Stables is open at peak times to serve small bites, hot chocolate and real fruit ice cream. Don’t forget to roast a marshmallow over the fire. 

The blossoms are for everyone — families, groups, date nights, and even four-legged friends on select days. You can book a professional photoshoot to capture your time together or reserve a golf cart to explore the grounds with ease. Family passes, discounted weekday tickets, and lush onsite accommodation are all available. Book ahead to avoid disappointment. The blossom season is short and sweet.

name: Diwali Festival of Lights
long_description:
The Diwali Festival of Lights is celebrated annually by Hindus, Jains, Sikhs and some Buddhists. Wellington's waterfront hosts the city's own Diwali on 25 October. Bring the whole whānau along to this free festival from 2pm to 8:30pm at TSB Arena and Shed 6. There will be non-stop entertainment and cultural activities including dance and music throughout the day. In between performances, grab a mango lassi and vegetarian kai options from across the region. Select a henna design for your hand or fashion and browse jewellery and fashion stalls.

Beyond stalls and stages, Diwali symbolises the ‘victory of light over darkness, good over evil, and knowledge over ignorance.’ To mark the celebration, the festival finishes with a fireworks display. Gather around Queens Wharf or along the Wellington Waterfront at 8:50pm to celebrate the end of a vibrant day of culture.

id: Flight of the Conchords-Michael Fowler Centre, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
name: Flight of the Conchords
venue: Michael Fowler Centre, Wellington, New Zealand
long_description:
Almost thirty years after the duo cut their teeth in the comedy clubs of Wellington, Flight of the Conchords are coming home. Fans can expect a career-spanning set. It will include hits from their Emmy-nominated HBO series and two critically acclaimed studio albums. 

After taking an eight-year break from performing, Bret McKenzie and Jemaine Clement burst back onto the live scene in 2026. They played two sold-out shows at Los Angeles’ Greek Theatre. That followed five intimate warm-up shows at Wellington’s Meow Nui. While they put the Conchords on ice for a few years, the pair both remained busy. Bret won an Academy Award for Best Original Song for ‘Man or Muppet’, wrote songs for ‘The Simpsons’ and‘The Minecraft Movie’, and released two solo albums. Jemaine has focused on the screen, creating comedy horror TV shows ‘Wellington Paranormal’ and ‘What We Do In The Shadows’. He’s also appeared in films including the last two ‘Avatar’ instalments. 

Don’t just think about it, get your tickets before they’re gone.

id: Sunset Boulevard-Te Whare Whakarauika Wellington Town Hall-Wellington NZ
name: Sunset Boulevard
venue: Te Whare Whakarauika Wellington Town Hall
long_description:
The New Zealand professional premiere of one of Andrew Lloyd Webber’s most celebrated musicals is coming to Wellington. Sunset Boulevard takes centre stage at the newly restored Wellington Town Hall in April. Local company WITCH Music Theatre is presenting an epic site-specific production as part of the venue’s grand reopening programme. 

In a major coup for the production, acclaimed Tony Award-nominated performer Keala Settle will be playing the main role, Norma Desmond. Keala has strong iwi links to New Zealand so she sees this opportunity as a homecoming. She is best known for her role as Lettie Lutz in ‘The Greatest Showman’ and for her powerhouse performance of the Golden Globe-winning song “This Is Me” from the film. 

Sunset Boulevard has earned major acclaim across Broadway and the West End, including seven awards from 11 Tony Award nominations for its original 1994 Broadway production. It’s 2023 revival won seven Olivier Awards from 11 nominations. The production, designed specifically for the Town Hall’s refurbished auditorium, marks the New Zealand professional premiere of the musical.

name: Verb Wellington Literary Festival
long_description:
Welcome in spring with a literary bonanza at Wellington’s iconic readers and writers’ festival. Verb has supported and nurtured Wellington’s arts community since its founding, and its annual festival has become a highlight of the literary calendar. Over three days, writers from across Aotearoa and several from around the world will share their ideas and stories with curious readers. Verb 2026 will be jam-packed with writers’ talks, workshops and panel discussions. 

Taking place from 23 to 27 September, Verb is a celebration of the written word and the community that surrounds it. See their website for a full list of the festival and special events.

id: Race Of Champions-Hnry Stadium, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
name: Race Of Champions
long_description:
Race Of Champions is an internationally renowned event. Winners from a range of racing disciplines go head-to-head on a purpose-built tarmac circuit constructed inside Hnry Stadium. Unlike traditional motorsport events, every driver competes in identical cars, putting the focus firmly on skill behind the wheel. 

The first drivers confirmed for Wellington include four-time Formula 1 World Champion Sebastian Vettel and Formula 1 race winner Valtteri Bottas. Supercars champion Chaz Mostert and New Zealand rally star Hayden Paddon are also coming. More competitors are to be announced for this Wellington exclusive event. 

Since its launch in 1988, Race Of Champions has brought together stars from Formula 1, World Rally Championship, IndyCar, NASCAR, Le Mans, and other top-tier racing series. Previous competitors have included Fernando Alonso, Lando Norris, Valentino Rossi, Mika Häkkinen, and Michael Schumacher.

id: 100 Years of Unity through Sport — New Zealand and India-Frank Kitts Park, Wellington, New Zealand-Wellington NZ
name: 100 Years of Unity through Sport — New Zealand and India
venue: Frank Kitts Park, Wellington, New Zealand
long_description:
This spring, Wellington will celebrate 100 years of sporting connection between India and New Zealand. The city will showcase its strong Indian community and cultural connections. This century milestone traces back to 1926, when an Indian Army hockey team toured New Zealand for the first time, bringing players and communities together. Since then, sport has played an important role in connecting our countries — notably through hockey and cricket, but also across many other sports and exchanges. 

From 23 October to 15 November, Frank Kitts Park and the waterfront promenade will host a free public exhibition. Light Box Historic Walk will feature 10 illuminated light boxes that share stories of Wellington-specific links between India and New Zealand. You’ll also find The Fan Hub on 6 and 7 November as well as 14 and 15 November. Enjoy a feast with local food truck favourites, offering a taste of Wellington's rich culinary scene. Or start the day with sunrise yoga sessions hosted by AWHI Yoga against the stunning waterfront backdrop. To cap off all the excitement, the BLACKCAPS take on India three times in Wellington as part of their summer season.

The Sport100 Fan Hub is proudly delivered through collaboration between WellingtonNZ, Sport New Zealand, Wellington City Council, Cricket Wellington, and New Zealand Cricket, creating a festive gathering place for locals and visitors to connect, celebrate, and enjoy the atmosphere whilst Wellington hosts cricketing giants India in the capital.
